title: CILIARY DYSKINESIA, PRIMARY, 2
alt_titles: CILIARY DYSKINESIA, PRIMARY, 2, WITH OR WITHOUT SITUS INVERSUS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that primary ciliary dyskinesia-2 (CILD2) is caused by homozygous mutation in the DNAAF3 gene (614566) on chromosome 19q13.

checks.explanation: Homozygous DNAAF3 mutations in families linked to the CILD2 locus.

checks.evidence_quote: The human DAB1 orthologous gene DNAAF3 on human chromosome 19q13 (previously designated C19orf51) encodes a 588 amino acid protein

paragraphs.text: Primary ciliary dyskinesia (PCD) is an autosomal recessive disorder of defective ciliary function. It is characterized by chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and subfertility. Situs inversus occurs in 50% of cases, a combination known as Kartagener syndrome. The ciliary defect is associated with ultrastructural abnormalities such as absent dynein arms, absent radial spokes, and disturbed ciliary orientation (Meeks et al., 2000). In CILD2, respiratory cilia are immotile and both outer and inner dynein arms are reduced or absent (Mitchison et al., 2012).

checks.explanation: The abstract calls it autosomal recessive and says the phenotype is caused by defective ciliary function.

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) reported 10 PCD patients with DNAAF3 mutations, 4 of whom had situs inversus. The patients came from 2 consanguineous families of Arabic origin (UCL89 and UCL66/67) and 1 consanguineous UK-Pakistani family (UCL71) from a first-cousin union. All had classic PCD symptoms, including neonatal respiratory distress, recurrent cough, wheezing and chest infections, sinusitis, otitis media, nasal polyps, and bronchiectasis. Respiratory cilia were immotile in all affected family members. Electron microscopy showed reduced or absent inner and outer dynein arms. In family UCL89, transmission electron microscopy of cilia cross sections showed loss of both outer and inner dynein arms in affected individuals.

paragraphs.text: In affected members of 2 of the 3 Arabic families originally linked to the CILD2 locus on chromosome 19q, Mitchison et al. (2012) identified homozygous mutations in the DNAAF3 gene. Affected individuals in both families showed large regions of marker homozygosity across the DNAAF3 locus. The mutations were a missense mutation (L108P) in family UCL89 and a nonsense mutation (R136X) in family UCL66/67. Mitchison et al. (2012) also sequenced DNAAF3 in 112 additional PCD families. In a consanguineous UK-Pakistani family (UCL71) showing evidence of linkage, they found a homozygous 1-bp insertion (c.762_763insT) that was predicted to cause a frameshift (V255CfsX12). For all 3 mutations, affected individuals were homozygous and unaffected parents and sibs were heterozygous. None of the mutations was found in population-matched control chromosomes or in the dbSNP, 1000 Genomes, or NHLBI-ESP databases. Mitchison et al. (2012) also found a homozygous c.973G-A substitution (A325T) in a Belgian patient with PCD (OP-549). Because this residue is not conserved, they considered the variant likely to be a Caucasian polymorphism.

paragraphs.text: In respiratory cells from patients with DNAAF3 mutations, Mitchison et al. (2012) found that the outer dynein arm proteins DNAH5, DNAH9, and DNAI2 and the inner dynein arm light chain DNALI1 were absent from cilia. This suggested that DNAAF3 is needed to assemble outer and inner dynein arms along the full length of the axoneme. In some patients, residual DNAH5 and DNALI1 accumulated in the apical cytoplasm. In Chlamydomonas, tagged PF22 protein, the DNAAF3 ortholog, was located only in the cytoplasm. In pf22 cytoplasm, the outer arm intermediate chain IC2 was over-abundant and an HC-beta epitope was inaccessible, while dynein heavy chain folding was less disturbed than in pf13 or oda7 mutants. The authors suggested that PF22/DNAAF3 acts at a later step of cytoplasmic dynein preassembly than PF13/DNAAF1 and ODA7/DNAAF2, such as joining heavy chains with smaller subunits.

paragraphs.text: Mitchison et al. (2012) found that morpholino knockdown of dnaaf3 in zebrafish made olfactory placode cilia immotile and caused loss of outer and inner dynein arms. Morphants also showed body axis curvature, hydrocephalus, pronephric cysts, otolith defects, and left-right patterning defects. About half of dnaaf3MOex8 embryos had reversed or absent heart looping.
